listing.scenes_note: apt_0..apt_5 (furnished with ~113-120 small objects), empty_stage, and 84 v3_sc{0-3}_staging_NN furniture-only layouts. All 90 non-empty scenes place fridge, kitchen_counter, kitchenCupboard_01, chestOfDrawers_01, cabinet, and door2; door1, door3, and doubledoor are never placed. The cabinet position changes between layouts.
listing.rooms_note: ReplicaCAD scenes have no room labels. Rooms here are open-plan zones read from apt_0 positions: kitchen (counter, cupboards, fridge along x=-2.3), entryway (shoes, rack, umbrella, hooks, chest of drawers, door2 at z=-2.65), office corner (table_01 + monitor), dining area (table_02), living area (sofa, TV stand, bookshelves wall_cabinet_01/02).

ycb_relation.summary: None of the 92 ReplicaCAD objects is YCB-derived: all are artist recreations of objects in the scanned Replica FRL apartment (asset names frl_apartment_*). Habitat 2.0 rearrangement tasks add YCB clutter from the separate dataset ai-habitat/ycb (CC BY 4.0, revision 29be64fdd95b4881f244152ad653058e0a48c28f, 77 object configs). Tasks can reuse existing atlas ycb_* ObjectInstances directly for those 77; ycb_equivalent_id on a candidate marks only a functional stand-in (same object class, different mesh).
ycb_relation.habitat_ycb_missing_from_atlas_reuse: ai-habitat/ycb lacks 001, 020, 022, 023, 027, 034, 039, 041, 045-047, 049, 060, 064, 066-069, 074-076; ideas here use only YCB objects present in it (ycb_027_skillet appears only as a functional equivalent).

functional_equivalents.frl_apartment_sponge_dish: ycb_026_sponge (holder only; the sponge itself comes from YCB)

notes: Brainstorm list, not reviewed tasks. Scenes reuse active scene ids. identity_note marks unlabelled assets whose identity is inferred from mesh bounds (cm) and mass; confirm before drafting. ReplicaCAD articulations are simulator joints with no latches or appliance states, so goals are joint positions (closed = joint at lower limit) and object-in-receptacle relations. Habitat 2.0 HAB task patterns (TidyHouse, PrepareGroceries, SetTable) are cited where an idea follows them.
